events.title: Magellan's Fleet Sets Sail from Seville
events.description: Ferdinand Magellan led five ships out of Seville. They were bound for the Spice Islands by a western route. Magellan was killed in the Philippines in 1521. Juan Sebastián Elcano took command and brought the expedition home.
events.significance: The voyage became the first circumnavigation of the globe. It proved the world could be sailed around and changed how people understood its size.

events.title: Storming of the Tuileries Palace
events.description: A Parisian crowd and revolutionary militia attacked the Tuileries Palace during the French Revolution. King Louis XVI was taken into custody and his Swiss Guards were massacred.
events.significance: The attack effectively ended the French monarchy. It led to the establishment of the First French Republic.

events.title: Missouri Becomes the 24th U.S. State
events.description: Missouri was admitted to the Union after the Missouri Compromise debates. The compromise allowed it in as a slave state and Maine in as a free state.
events.significance: Missouri's admission was a key moment in the national struggle over slavery. It also opened the way for westward expansion.

events.title: Smithsonian Institution Is Chartered
events.description: President James K. Polk signed the act creating the Smithsonian Institution. The act used a bequest from British scientist James Smithson, who had never visited the United States.
events.significance: The Smithsonian grew into the world's largest museum and research complex. It is a national center for education, science, and culture.
